questions.stem:
A particle $P$ moves along a straight line. The fixed point $O$ is on the line. At time $t$ seconds, $t>0$, the displacement of $P$ from $O$ is $x$ metres, where
$x = 2t^3-21t^2+60t$
Find

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) the values of $t$ for which $P$ is instantaneously at rest
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Use of $v=\frac{dx}{dt}$. At least 2 powers going down by 1. Clear division by $t$ is M0
A1: $v=6t^2-42t+60$ Correct only
M1: Set $v=0$ and correctly solves to obtain 2 values for $t$ (implied by correct answers seen) $(0=t^2-7t+10=(t-2)(t-5))$
A1: Obtain $t=2$ and $t=5$ Correct only. Allow 2.0, 5.0

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) the distance travelled by $P$ in the interval $1\leqslant t\leqslant 3$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Distance $=|x_2-x_1|+|x_3-x_2|$ $(=|45-52|+|52-41|)$ Correct strategy dependent on their $t$ being in $1<t<3$
A1: $=11+7=18$ (m) Correct only

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at the instant when $t=3$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Use of $a=\frac{dv}{dt}$. Differentiate their $v$. Clear division by $t$ is M0. A power going down by 1 $(a=12t-42)$
A1: Obtain $6\,(\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}})$ Must be positive – the Q asks for magnitude

questions.stem:
Figure 5 shows a uniform beam $AB$, of weight $40\,\mathrm{N}$ and length $7\,\mathrm{m}$, resting with end $A$ on rough horizontal ground.
The beam rests on a smooth horizontal peg at $C$, with $AC=5\,\mathrm{m}$, as shown in Figure 5.
The beam is inclined at an angle $\theta$ to the ground, where $\sin\theta = \frac{3}{5}$
The beam is modelled as a rod that lies in a vertical plane perpendicular to the peg.
The normal reaction between the beam and the peg at $C$ has magnitude $P$ newtons.
Using the model,

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Moments about $A$: Dimensionally correct. Condone sine / cosine confusion
A1: $5P=40\times\frac{7}{2}\cos\theta$ Correct unsimplified equation
A1*: $P=22.4$ Obtain given answer from correct working. Need to see evidence of $\cos\theta=\frac{4}{5}$

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) find the magnitude of the resultant force acting on the beam at $A$.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
Two equations required. M1A1 for the first equation seen, M1A1 for the second equation. If more than 2 equations mark the two equations used to obtain the resultant, or the best 2 if they do not go on to find the resultant.
M1: First equation, e.g. Resolve horizontally. Condone sine / cosine confusion
A1: $H=P\sin\theta$ $(=13.44)$ Correct unsimplified equation
M1: Second equation, e.g. Resolve vertically. Condone sine / cosine confusion
A1: $V+P\cos\theta=40$ $(V=22.08)$ Correct unsimplified equation
DM1: $|R|=\sqrt{H^2+V^2}$ solve for $|R|$. Dependent on the 2 preceding Ms
A1: $|R|=26$ (N) Or better (25.84879…) Accept $\frac{24\sqrt{29}}{5}$
Alternative (parallel/perpendicular resolution):
M1: First equation, e.g. Resolve parallel. Condone sine / cosine confusion
A1: $X=40\sin\theta$ $(=24)$ Correct unsimplified equation
M1: Second equation, e.g. Resolve perpendicular. Condone sine / cosine confusion
A1: $Y+P=40\cos\theta$ $(Y=9.6)$ Correct unsimplified equation
DM1: $|R|=\sqrt{X^2+Y^2}$ solve for $|R|$. Dependent on the 2 preceding Ms
A1: $|R|=26$ (N) Or better (25.84879…) Accept $\frac{24\sqrt{29}}{5}$
Alternative moments equations: M(C) $40\times 1.5\cos\theta+H\times 5\sin\theta=V\times 5\cos\theta$; M(B) $2P+7\cos\theta\times V=7\sin\theta\times H+3.5\times 40\cos\theta$; M(G) $1.5P+3.5\sin\theta\times H=3.5\cos\theta\times V$
Alternative (triangle of forces / cosine rule):
M1: 3 force diagram seen or implied
A1: Forces and angle in correct positions
M1: Use Cosine Rule. Correct formula used
A1: $(|R|)^2=40^2+22.4^2-2\times 40\times 22.4\cos\theta$ Correct unsimplified equation
DM1: Substitute for trig and solve for $|R|$. Dependent on the 2 preceding Ms
A1: $|R|=26$ (N) Or better (25.84879…) Accept $\frac{24\sqrt{29}}{5}$

questions.stem:
[In this question $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ are unit vectors, with $\mathbf{i}$ horizontal and $\mathbf{j}$ vertical.]
The fixed points $A$ and $B$ lie on horizontal ground.
At time $t=0$, a particle $P$ is projected from $A$ with velocity $(4\mathbf{i}+7\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$
Particle $P$ moves freely under gravity and hits the ground at $B$, as shown in Figure 6.

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Use symmetry to find time taken: $-7=7-gt$ Or equivalent complete method using suvat to find the time taken e.g. find the time for vertical distance $=0$
A1: $t=\frac{14}{g}\,(=1.428…)$ Correct value seen or implied
DM1: Horizontal distance $=4t$ Complete method using suvat to find the distance. Dependent on the preceding M1
A1: $=5.71$ (m) or $5.7$ (m) 3 sf or 2 sf only $\frac{40}{7}$ scores A0; $\frac{56}{g}$ scores A0 (incorrect units)
Alternative:
M1: Find speed and angle of projection. Correct use of Pythagoras and trig.
A1: Speed $=\sqrt{16+49}=\sqrt{65}\,(\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}})$ Direction $=\tan^{-1}\frac{7}{4}\,(=60.3^\circ)$ Both values seen or implied
DM1: Use of $R=\frac{u^2\sin 2\alpha}{g}$ Or equivalent. Dependent on the preceding M1
A1: $=5.71$ (m) or $5.7$ (m) 3 sf or 2 sf only

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The speed of $P$ is less than $5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ for an interval of length $T$ seconds.
(b) Find the value of $T$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: $|v|=5\Rightarrow v=4\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}$ or $v=4\mathbf{i}-3\mathbf{j}$ Correct vertical component seen or implied
M1: Complete method to find $T$ e.g. $T=\frac{14}{g}-2\times\frac{4}{g}$
A1: $T=0.612$ or $T=0.61$ 3 sf or 2 sf only $\frac{30}{49}$ scores A0; $\frac{6}{g}$ scores A0 (incorrect units)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1: $-3=3-gT$

parts.label: c
parts.text:
At the instant when the direction of motion of $P$ is perpendicular to the initial direction of motion of $P$, the particle is $h$ metres above the ground.
(c) Find the value of $h$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $\begin{pmatrix}4\\7\end{pmatrix}\cdot\begin{pmatrix}4\\p\end{pmatrix}=0$ Or equivalent method to find perpendicular velocity
A1: $\Rightarrow p=-\frac{16}{7}$, $v=4\mathbf{i}-\frac{16}{7}\mathbf{j}$ Correct vertical component. Allow $-2.28…$
DM1: $\left(-\frac{16}{7}\right)^2=7^2-2gh$ Complete method using suvat or energy to form an equation in $h$ only. Dependent on the preceding M1
A1: $h=2.23$ or $h=2.2$ 3 sf or 2 sf only cso (negative vertical component seen at some point)
Alternative:
M1: $\begin{pmatrix}4\\7\end{pmatrix}\cdot\begin{pmatrix}4\\7-gt\end{pmatrix}=0$ Or equivalent method to find time when velocity perpendicular
A1: $t=\frac{65}{7g}\,(=0.947…)$ Correct time
DM1: $h=7t-\frac{1}{2}gt^2$ Complete method using suvat to form an equation in $h$ only
A1: $h=2.23$ or $h=2.2$ 3 sf or 2 sf only cso
